study: Song et al. 2021 / Garet et al. 2017 — Impact of Providing Performance Feedback to Teachers and Principals (NCEE 2018-4001, AIR)
eval_evidence: Independent NCEE/IES evaluation conducted by AIR (Garet, Wayne, Brown, Rickles, Song, Manzeske); a large-scale randomized experiment run by the IES contractor, not a program developer with a stake.
developer_evidence: The intervention components (classroom-observation ratings via CLASS/FFT, value-added growth reports, 360 principal survey) were produced and delivered by the study/research team: ratings 'coded by trained observers on the study research team'; study-hired observers fed back to educators.
cascade_evidence: Study research-team observers rated classrooms and the project delivered feedback reports directly to teachers/principals; no train-the-trainer intermediary between the research team and educators.
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools continued the standard district feedback/evaluation process (business as usual); treatment educators reported receiving more/more-frequent feedback than controls, as intended.
coaching_evidence: Intervention is performance FEEDBACK, not coaching; the report explicitly notes 'non-school-based observers excluded coaches or mentors' — observers did not 'support, plan professional development, or guide coaching'. No in-class coaching component.
student_dose_evidence: A teacher/principal-facing feedback program; students receive only the teacher's regular instruction — no tutoring, pull-out, or added student-facing dose.
maturity_evidence: Two-year program (2012-13 and 2013-14); the extracted end-of-treatment wave is post-Year-2 (spring 2014), measured after a full prior implementation year, so teachers/principals were experienced with the feedback system.
